scorecard.note: Create clearer, simpler visuals that are easily readable on a phone screen.

storyboard.ears: Routine infections are learning to outlast the medicines built to stop them.
Drug resistance directly killed 1.27 million people in 2019. Routine infections already carry a major global toll.
storyboard.eyes: substance: lit apartment windows; cause: Data pulls the city's breaker lever down and the resistance share of its windows goes dark
storyboard.evidence: The Lancet | Global deaths linked to antibiotic-resistant infections, 2019 (millions) | https://www.thelancet.com | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: Resistance deaths could reach 10 million yearly by 2050. Today's toll is only the start of the projected rise.
storyboard.evidence: UK Government-commissioned review | Global deaths from drug-resistant infections, actual vs. 2050 projection (millions) | https://amr-review.org | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: Projected resistance deaths match 10 million current cancer deaths yearly. The future toll would be cancer-sized.
storyboard.evidence: O'Neill Review on AMR / World Health Organization | Projected 2050 drug-resistance deaths vs. current global cancer deaths (millions/year) | https://amr-review.org | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: Preserving effective antibiotics protects ordinary medical care from becoming far more dangerous.
